## ✨ Added

- **Start, end and duration on the Dashboard's Last Backups.** (#39, thanks @ptmorris1) Each entry now shows when the backup started and finished, with the elapsed time.
- **Search and filters on the Containers and VMs views.** (#40 / #41, thanks @ptmorris1) A search box to find a container/VM by name, plus filter chips for **scheduled / not scheduled** and **backed up / never backed up**. Filters persist per browser and combine with the sort and the installed/orphan view. (Selecting rows then filtering now also prunes any hidden rows from the selection, so a bulk action never touches something you can't see.)

## 🎨 Design

- **The Automatic restore-check schedule now lives in Plans**, next to the backup schedules, instead of tucked away in Settings. (#42, thanks @manilx)
- **Clarified the flash zip export "Keep history" wording** so it's clear that setting is separate from the restic retention: off keeps a single, always-overwritten file (so the destination never fills), on keeps the newest N. (#43, thanks @manilx)

## Fixed

- **A not-installed container that still has backups no longer shows "Last backup: Never".** (#44, thanks @manilx) When Discover rebuilds an entry from backups already in the repository, that entry has no run history, so its "Last backup" read "Never" even though snapshots clearly existed. It now falls back to the newest snapshot's actual date. (These entries appear because Discover, the disaster-recovery button, re-adds any container that still has backups in the repo so you can restore or delete them; "Delete all backups" on the entry clears it.)

---

- **The Recovery tab's readability check no longer resurrects deleted-container entries.** (#44, thanks @manilx) When you removed a container that BombVault had backed up (for example, swapping a Docker container for a plugin), a "not installed" orphan entry could reappear on the Containers page "out of nowhere" — without anyone clicking **Discover backups**. The cause: the Recovery tab's "is my backup readable?" check (Step 1 *Re-check* / Step 2 *Connect & preview*) ran `discover` purely as a probe, but `discover` has a write side-effect — it rebuilds the target list from the backups still in the repository. So merely checking readability silently re-added every container that still had a backup sitting in the repo. The readability check is now **read-only**: it opens and decrypts the repository to confirm it is reachable and your `APP_KEY` is correct, but writes nothing. Only the explicit **Discover backups** action (Containers/VMs page, or Recovery Step 3) rebuilds targets.

v4.9.1 already fixed the misleading "Last backup: Never" on these rows; to remove a leftover entry for good, use **Delete all backups** on it.

---

*Also includes what was previously released separately as 4.9.1, 4.9.2.*
